title: Model staging: circuit breakers & rollback plan for speculative decoding
content:
Purpose and scope:

This doc describes a pragmatic staging and safety plan for onboarding model variants that enable speculative decoding (spec-decode) and associated kernel routing / KV cache changes. The goal is to provide deterministic acceptance criteria, circuit-breaker definitions, telemetry signatures for regressions, and a scripted rollback path so that model/engine teams can roll a candidate into production with measurable risk control.

Key goals:
- Protect production SLAs (latency, availability) while testing spec-decode behaviors.
- Detect correctness/regression signals early (response divergence, hallucination spikes, quality drop).
- Limit blast radius with incremental ramps and automated fallback.
- Capture telemetry and traces that allow root cause: kernel selection, KV-miss patterns, and batch scheduling artifacts.

Phased rollout model:
1) Dark stage (internal traffic only) – run candidate alongside current runtime but do not serve to external customers. Collect full telemetry including reference outputs and KV access patterns. Verify resource behaviour (GPU utilization, kernel time, memory, KV eviction).
2) Canary stage (1–2% of production traffic, pinned set of customers) – route a tiny fraction of live traffic through the candidate with hedged fallback to primary path for every request. Monitor soft and hard thresholds; auto-fallback on circuit-breaker triggers.
3) Ramp stage (progressive increases 2% -> 10% -> 30%) – step increases gated by acceptance windows and manual/automated approvals.
4) Full rollout or retire – either promote candidate as default, keep as opt-in variant, or rollback and iterate.

Circuit breaker taxonomy (what to protect):
- Latency SLO breach (hard): if candidate increases p95 request latency by > 200ms absolute or > 30% relative for 5m window, trigger immediate fallback for new requests and reduce canary allocation to 0.
- Error spike (hard): 5xxs or model runtime exceptions > 0.5% of requests over 1m window triggers fallback and alert.
- KV-miss avalanche (operational): sudden increase in KV read miss rate (> 4x baseline sustained for 2m) — throttle speculative prefetching, reduce batch sizes, degrade to non-speculative path if remains.
- Divergence index (quality): fraction of responses where token-level edit distance to reference > threshold or top-k token disagreement > 0.4 for > 1% of canary requests over 15m. Trigger pause and human review.
- Hallucination / toxicity signals (quality): if safety classifiers or eval-suite fail rate increases by > 50% relative to baseline over sliding 30m, immediately route traffic away and create high-priority incident.

Telemetry & metrics (minimum required):
Operational metrics (per-model-variant, per-region):
- request.count (string)
- request.latency.p50/p95/p99 (ms)
- request.errors.5xx (count)
- kernel.exec_time.mean/p95 (ms)
- kernel.selection.count.{kernel_name} (count)
- kv.cache.hit_rate (ratio)
- kv.cache.evictions_per_minute (count)
- kv.read_latency.p50/p95 (ms)
- speculative.prefetch.requests (count)
- speculative.prefetch.success_rate (ratio)
- speculative.rollback.count (count) — number of requests where fallback occurred due to speculative path failure

Quality metrics (per-candidate-window):
- divergence.rate (fraction) — compare candidate output to production reference (exact match, token-level edit distance, semantic similarity).
- eval-suite.fail_rate (fraction) — results from offline prompt set evaluation (critical prompts).
- user-reported-regressions (count) — from telemetry + CS intake.
- safety.failures (count) — safety classifier triggers.

Metric windows and baselines:
- Baseline calculations: use rolling 7d median for stable baselines; use 1h baseline for short-lived experiments.
- Windows: p95 and error thresholds evaluated over 5m, 15m, and 60m sliding windows. Quality windows default 15m and 60m; can use 24h for long-running ramps.

Acceptance criteria (example):
- Latency: candidate p95 <= baseline p95 + 150ms and relative p95 increase <= 20% over 15m window.
- Errors: candidate 5xx <= baseline 5xx + 0.1% (absolute) over 15m window.
- KV: candidate kv.hit_rate >= baseline - 3% and kv.evictions_per_minute not > 2x baseline.
- Divergence: divergence.rate <= 0.5% on critical prompt set; semantic-similarity median >= baseline median - 0.03.
- Safety: eval-suite.fail_rate <= baseline fail_rate * 1.2 (no more than 20% relative increase).

Automated rollback & fallback behavior:
- Soft fallback: for non-critical threshold breaches (minor latency increase, small kv miss spikes), the runtime will dynamically reduce canary weight by 50% and enable hedged fallback for affected requests for 10m.
- Hard rollback: on hard circuit-breaker triggers (latency hard, error spike, safety), immediately set canary allocation to 0, route all new traffic to previous production variant, and create an incident with tag "spec-decode-rollback".
- Non-destructive rollback: ensure KV invariants are maintained — candidate writes to KV must be idempotent or write-ahead (do not evict live entries). If candidate performs speculative writes to shared caches, write isolation must be enforced in staging canaries.

Kernel & scheduler-specific checks:
- Kernel churn: track kernel.selection.count and kernel.exec_time per kernel. If the candidate causes >40% increase in kernel switch frequency per-request, expect increased latency variance; fail canary if latency criteria breached.
- Batch size distribution: ensure batch sizes remain within expected distribution; a sudden shift to smaller/bigger batches indicates scheduler mis-routing. Add histogram metric: scheduler.batch_size.histogram.
- KV locality: measure kv.cache.hit_rate split by prefix/namespace. If candidate increases misses for hot prefixes, consider per-namespace throttles.

Operational runbook (on alert):
1) Pager fires with tag spec-decode-ops. Triage dashboard: canary allocation, p95 latency, 5xx rate, kv.hit_rate, divergence.rate, kernel.exec_time.
2) If hard trigger: execute automated hard rollback and notify on-call + product leads. Post-rollback, collect 30m of traces and save a snapshot (trace ids, sample ids) for RCA.
3) If soft trigger: reduce allocation by 50%, open a review thread with triage notes, and enable extended logging for a 30m window.
4) For quality triggers (divergence/safety): capture sample request/response pairs (anonymized), attach to ticket, and pause ramp pending human review.

Data collection & privacy:
- Only capture minimal request metadata for production users (request id, timestamps, model variant, kernel id) in logs. Do not store full user inputs unless explicitly opted-in or for internal test tenants. Samples captured for QA must be scrubbed per PII policy and marked "review-scrubbed".

Smoke tests and preflight checklist (before canary):
- Unit performance: kernel.exec_time per-op within 10% of expectation on representative hardware.
- KV stress: run 30m KV stress harness reproducing steady-state traffic, assert kv.hit_rate remains >= baseline-2%.
- Logical correctness: run critical prompt set (100 prompts) with golden outputs; divergence.rate <= 0.2%.
- Resource safety: GPU memory growth linear, no unbounded allocations, no OOM across 1h soak at 2x expected qps.
- Rollback dry-run: simulate a rollback and validate no orphaned speculative cache entries remain.

Experiment tagging & metadata conventions:
- model_variant tag format: model-name@sha (e.g., redwood-1.1@abc1234)
- staging_session_id: use UUID for each staged rollout to correlate telemetry.
- kernel_tag: kernel-name:version

Documentation & handover:
- Every canary must be accompanied by a short "canary brief" (one-pager) with: intent, smoke test results, baseline pointers, risk matrix, quick rollback steps, and contact list. Store in shared drive under path: shared_drives/engineering/serving-runtime/canary-briefs/

Open questions & follow-ups:
- Should speculative prefetched KV writes be fully isolated per-customer during canary, or can we allow write-through with compensating cleanup? (security/consistency tradeoff)
- Investigate automated semantic similarity metric that runs in ~real-time at low cost (embedding sampling vs. full-run).
- Define retention period for canary traces (default 30d?) and who can access them.

Appendix: quick alert queries (examples):
- High p95 delta: (candidate.request.latency.p95 - baseline.request.latency.p95) > 150ms over 5m
- KV miss storm: candidate.kv.cache.hit_rate < baseline.kv.cache.hit_rate * 0.75 for 2m
- Divergence spike: candidate.divergence.count / candidate.request.count > 0.01 over 15m

Summary:
This plan prioritizes protecting customers while allowing the runtime and model teams to evaluate speculative decoding optimizations in production-like conditions. The combination of phased rollouts, well-defined circuit-breakers, and explicit telemetry should reduce time-to-signal for regressions and make rollbacks predictable and low-friction.

Notes to reviewers:
- Please review acceptance thresholds and suggest conservative adjustments for high-traffic regions.
- Add any missing telemetry that you rely on when debugging kernel or KV issues.

Authors: Aisha Menon (lead), Diego Alvarez (kernel), Maya Chen (kv/cache), Priya Singh (QA)
summary: Staging and safety plan for onboarding speculative decoding + runtime kernel and KV changes, including circuit breakers, metrics and rollback procedures.
